message.content:
I’m happy to show you how to add that comment.  
Below is the exact `curl` command you can run from a terminal (or use any HTTP client you prefer).  

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

**What this does**

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` | Creates a new comment on the IP resource. |
| `-H "x-apikey: ABC321"` | Authenticates your request with your API key. |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells VirusTotal that the body is JSON. |
| `-d '{...}'` | The JSON payload you supplied. |

**Response**

If everything is correct, you’ll receive a `201 Created` response with a JSON body that includes the newly‑created comment’s ID and other metadata.  
If there’s an error (e.g., invalid key, rate‑limit exceeded, malformed JSON), you’ll get a `4xx` or `5xx` status code with an error message.

---

### Quick sanity check

If you want to verify that the comment was added, you can fetch the comments for that IP:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321"
```

Look for an entry with `"text": "Confirmed #malware"` in the returned list.

---

**Note:**  
I don’t have the ability to execute the request myself, so you’ll need to run the command in your own environment. If you hit any issues, let me know the exact error message and I can help troubleshoot!
